meta.spec_reference: Multimedia Programming Interface and Data Specifications 1.0 (IBM Corporation and Microsoft Corporation, August 1991) - the RIFF container and the WAVE form, including the fmt, data, fact, cue, LIST/INFO, LIST/adtl and LIST/wavl chunks; Microsoft WAVEFORMATEX and WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE (Windows SDK, mmreg.h) for the format tag registry and the 40-byte extensible format chunk; the RIFF WAVE sampler chunk definition as published in the MIDI Manufacturers Association DLS specifications for the smpl chunk; IMA/DVI ADPCM Recommended Practices for Enhancing Digital Audio Compatibility (IMA, 1992) for the wSamplesPerBlock relationship. The template itself cites https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WAV at line 17.

schema_extensions.name: present_when
schema_extensions.where: the six padding entries - FORMATCHUNK.padding, DATACHUNK.padding, LISTSUBCHUNK.padding, LISTCHUNK.padding, UNKNOWNCHUNK.padding and SMPLCHUNK.padding
schema_extensions.why: These bytes are typed fixed_value because they are padding pinned to zero, which the checklist requires, but their defining property is CONDITIONAL PRESENCE rather than value: the byte exists if and only if the enclosing chunk's size is odd. A generator that emits it unconditionally, or never, misaligns every chunk that follows. There is no schema key for conditional presence on a constraints entry, and burying it in a description string would put a structural rule in prose.

schema_extensions.name: fixed_result / fixed_result_hex
schema_extensions.where: the FORMATCHUNK.wcbsize, CUEPOINT.dwChunkStart, CUEPOINT.dwBlockStart and SMPLCHUNK.Sampler_Data entries
schema_extensions.why: Each of these is genuinely a derived quantity - a byte count or an offset - that nonetheless has exactly one correct value in the files this template can produce: 2 for the ADPCM extension, 0 for both cue offsets in a file with no wavl playlist, and 0 for the sampler data the template never reads. fixed_result records the constant so the rewrite step can emit it directly, while algorithm/covers/includes_self still document what the field measures.

schema_extensions.name: lookahead sub-keys: comparison, switch_line, case_line, tested_at_line
schema_extensions.where: the six chunk-identifier entries and the LISTCHUNK.subchunk entry
schema_extensions.why: The top-level dispatch peeks four bytes with ReadBytes at line 535 and switches on them at line 538, so the peek site and the six comparison sites are different lines - switch_line and case_line record both, which a single call_site_line cannot. Separately, the LIST loop's ReadUInt peek at line 166 is not compared against literals at all: it is a bounds test at line 167 deciding whether the next subchunk fits. That call site has no mined value set, so `values` is empty and `comparison` is bounds_test - without which a value-mining pass would either invent literals or skip the call entirely.

schema_extensions.name: lookahead function value "ReadUInt"
schema_extensions.why: The schema enumerates ReadUByte, ReadUShort, ReadByte and ReadBytes. This template also uses ReadUInt, at line 166 inside the LIST loop and at line 566 for the unknown-chunk diagnostic. Dropping the entry would lose the one lookahead in the file that bounds a repeating section.

schema_extensions.name: excluded_values
schema_extensions.why: This field is defined by exclusion: any printable four-character identifier EXCEPT the six the top-level dispatch already claims. A pattern_constraint expresses the character class but cannot express the hole, and emitting one of the six here would produce a chunk the template's own grammar re-parses with a different, often fixed-shape layout.

schema_extensions.name: byte_layout
schema_extensions.why: The 24-byte stride of a cue record and of a loop record is nowhere stated in the .bt - it is implicit in a struct definition elsewhere - and the rewrite step needs it to convert between an element count and the enclosing chunk size.

schema_extensions.name: template_deviations
schema_extensions.why: This template validates only the RIFF/WAVE signature and the presence of a format chunk, and it disagrees with the specification in fourteen concrete places: a length field whose bytes are never read, an ignored container size, signed declarations for every unsigned 32-bit field, two chunk structs missing their padding branch, a fact chunk read by shape rather than by length, three legal sample depths with no typed layout, an undecoded extensible format extension, and a subchunk loop with no progress guarantee. A generator that imitated the parser's laxity would emit files this template accepts and no audio tool does, so these must be visible as data rather than buried in prose.

meta.structure_note: A RIFF container with NO terminator: the 12-byte 'RIFF' + size + 'WAVE' header, then a flat stream of chunks each consisting of a four-character identifier, a 32-bit little-endian size, that many data bytes and a pad byte when the size is odd - of which 'fmt ' and 'data' are mandatory and 'fmt ' must come first, the stream ending when the container size is exhausted.

WAVRIFFHEADER.groupID.description: The RIFF container signature opening the file; the template aborts outright on anything else.
WAVRIFFHEADER.groupID.notes: Declared at line 29 and checked by the guard at lines 523-527, which calls Warning and returns -1. The template's own header records the file signature at line 10 as `52 49 46 46 [+4] 57 41 56 45`, i.e. 'RIFF' then any four bytes then 'WAVE'. RIFF also defines the big-endian container 'RIFX', which this template rejects. This is one of the two most important fixed values in the format and must never receive an evil value.

WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize.description: Size of the RIFF container's payload: everything in the file after the eight bytes of this header's identifier and size field.
WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize.algorithm: byte count = total file size minus 8
WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize.covers: the four riffType bytes plus every chunk in the file, including each chunk's identifier, size field, data and pad byte; it excludes the groupID field and this size field itself

generation_range.rationale: The floor of 36 is the smallest self-consistent WAVE: 4 for 'WAVE' plus a 24-byte PCM fmt chunk plus an 8-byte empty data chunk. A signed 32-bit field can claim 2 GB, and although this template never uses it for anything, every real reader trusts it to bound the chunk walk. Capping at 256 KB keeps generated audio files cheap.

WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize.notes: TEMPLATE DEVIATION: the field is read into the struct and then NEVER used - the top-level loop at line 532 walks chunks with `while( !FEof() )` rather than honouring this size, so a wrong value is invisible here and desynchronises a conforming reader. Declared `long`, which is signed, where RIFF specifies an unsigned 32-bit value.

WAVRIFFHEADER.riffType.description: The RIFF form type identifying this container as a WAVE file; checked together with the RIFF signature.
WAVRIFFHEADER.riffType.notes: Declared at line 31 and checked by the same guard at lines 523-527. RIFF containers use this field to distinguish WAVE from AVI, RMID and the other RIFF form types, so the pair 'RIFF' plus 'WAVE' is what actually identifies a .wav file. Together with groupID this is the format's complete signature.

FORMATCHUNK.chunkID.description: The four-character chunk identifier that marks this as the format chunk; the top-level dispatch selects this struct only when the peeked tag equals it.

lookahead.note: The top-level chunk dispatch reads the four tag bytes by lookahead at line 535 and switches on them at line 538; the six recognised literals are at lines 540, 544, 548, 552, 556 and 560, and anything else falls to the default at line 564. Because the peek does not advance the file position, the same four bytes are then consumed as this struct's chunkID.

FORMATCHUNK.chunkID.notes: RIFF chunk identifiers are exactly four bytes of printable ASCII, space-padded when the name is shorter - which is why 'fmt ' and 'cue ' carry a trailing space that is part of the identifier and must be emitted. This is the chunk that declares the sample format for the whole file, so the trailing space is load-bearing: 'fmt' with a NUL or any other fourth byte falls to the UNKNOWNCHUNK branch and the file is then rejected at line 70 for having no valid format chunk.

FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize.description: Byte count of this chunk's data, excluding the four identifier bytes and this size field itself and excluding any trailing pad byte.
FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize.algorithm: byte count = 16 for a plain PCM format chunk, 18 when a two-byte cbSize extension field is present, 20 for the DVI IMA ADPCM layout this template reads, and 40 for WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE
FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize.covers: the format fields following the size: wFormatTag, wChannels, dwSamplesPerSec, dwAvgBytesPerSec, wBlockAlign, wBitsPerSample and any extension bytes; it excludes the 'fmt ' identifier, this size field and any pad byte

generation_range.rationale: Unlike the data chunk this size is not free: the specification defines exactly four layouts, of 16, 18, 20 and 40 bytes. The template reads 16 bytes unconditionally, 4 more when wFormatTag is 17, and dumps any remainder into unknown[] at line 56 - so a size below 16 makes that subtraction negative while a size above 40 is not a layout any decoder knows.

FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize.notes: RIFF (Microsoft Multimedia Programming Interface and Data Specifications 1.0): every chunk is a four-character identifier, a 32-bit little-endian size, and that many data bytes, followed by a pad byte if the size is odd. The size counts neither the identifier nor itself nor the pad byte. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: declared as a SIGNED `long`, so a size above 2^31-1 reads negative and becomes a negative array bound. 16 is the value for the plain PCM chunk a generator should prefer.

FORMATCHUNK.wFormatTag.description: Audio format code declaring how the sample data is encoded; it decides whether the sample bytes are raw PCM or a compressed stream, and whether extension fields follow.
value_names: WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE - the real format is named by a GUID in the 40-byte extension
FORMATCHUNK.wFormatTag.notes: Declared at line 39 and tested at line 45, which is the template's only branch on it: `if (wFormatTag == 17) //DVI IMA ADPCM` adds the two extension fields. WAVE_FORMAT_PCM (1) is strongly preferred for generation - it is the only tag for which the sample bytes need no valid compressed stream, and it is the one every decoder implements. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: declared as a SIGNED `short`, so WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE (0xFFFE) reads as -2; and the template reads none of the 22 extension bytes that tag requires.

FORMATCHUNK.wChannels.description: Number of interleaved audio channels; it is the element count of every SAMPLES frame and a factor of the block alignment.

generation_range.rationale: Used directly as an array bound at lines 103, 105 and 107 with no check. A 16-bit channel count of 65535 makes each sample frame 128 KB at 16 bits per sample, and the frame array is then sized by chunkSize divided by wBlockAlign - so an inconsistent pair produces an enormous nested structure. 1 (mono) and 2 (stereo) are what real files use, and mono additionally reaches the template's three fast-path branches at lines 83, 88 and 93.

FORMATCHUNK.wChannels.notes: Declared at line 40 and compared against 1 at lines 83, 88 and 93 to select the flat-array fast paths. The specification requires at least one channel; zero channels makes wBlockAlign zero, which the data chunk guard at line 78 explicitly tests for because it would be a division by zero at line 108.

FORMATCHUNK.dwSamplesPerSec.description: Sampling rate in sample frames per second; it must be non-zero and is one of the two factors of the average byte rate.

generation_range.rationale: Real rates are 8000, 11025, 22050, 44100 and 48000. A 32-bit value near 4 billion makes dwAvgBytesPerSec - which must equal this times wBlockAlign - overflow its own 32-bit field, so the two cannot both be consistent at extreme values. It costs no file bytes but a player computing a duration from it will produce nonsense.

evidence.note: RIFF WAVE format chunk: 'dwSamplesPerSec - Sample rate, in samples per second (hertz).' A rate of zero describes audio that never advances and is a division by zero in any duration computation. The template reads a plain unsigned long and performs no check.

FORMATCHUNK.dwAvgBytesPerSec.description: Average data rate in bytes per second; for uncompressed PCM it is exactly the sampling rate times the block alignment, and a player uses it to size its buffers.
FORMATCHUNK.dwAvgBytesPerSec.algorithm: dwSamplesPerSec * wBlockAlign for uncompressed formats; for a compressed format it is the encoder's average output rate
FORMATCHUNK.dwAvgBytesPerSec.covers: nothing itself; it is a derived rate describing the data chunk's payload

generation_range.rationale: Must equal dwSamplesPerSec * wBlockAlign for PCM, so it is not a free value at all - the ceiling here is 48000 * 8, i.e. 48 kHz stereo 32-bit. Choosing it independently of the rate and the block alignment is the most common way a generated fmt chunk becomes internally inconsistent.

evidence.note: RIFF WAVE format chunk: 'dwAvgBytesPerSec - Average data rate. Playback software can estimate the buffer size using this value.' For WAVE_FORMAT_PCM it must equal dwSamplesPerSec times wBlockAlign. The template reads a plain unsigned long and performs no check.

FORMATCHUNK.wBlockAlign.description: Size in bytes of one complete sample frame across all channels; it is the divisor the data chunk uses to count frames, so a zero or inconsistent value breaks the whole sample parse.
FORMATCHUNK.wBlockAlign.algorithm: wChannels * wBitsPerSample / 8 for uncompressed formats; for a compressed format it is the encoder's block size
FORMATCHUNK.wBlockAlign.covers: nothing itself; it is the stride of one sample frame in the data chunk payload

generation_range.rationale: Must equal wChannels * wBitsPerSample / 8 for PCM, giving 1 for 8-bit mono through 8 for 32-bit stereo. It is used as a divisor at lines 78 and 108, which is exactly why the guard at line 78 tests it against zero: a zero block alignment would be a division by zero. An inconsistent non-zero value silently changes the frame count.

FORMATCHUNK.wBlockAlign.notes: Declared at line 43 and used three times in the data chunk: tested against 0 and used as a modulus at line 78, and used as the frame-count divisor at line 108. RIFF WAVE: 'wBlockAlign - The block alignment (in bytes) of the data ... Playback software needs to process a multiple of wBlockAlign bytes of data at a time.' The data chunk's size must be an exact multiple of it, which the template checks at line 78 and falls back to an opaque byte array when it fails.

FORMATCHUNK.wBitsPerSample.description: Bits in each individual sample of one channel; the template supports only 8, 16 and 32 and routes everything else to an opaque byte array.
FORMATCHUNK.wBitsPerSample.notes: Declared at line 44 and compared against 8, 16 and 32 five separate times: at line 77 to decide whether the samples are parseable at all, at lines 83, 88 and 93 for the mono fast paths, and at lines 102, 104 and 106 for the general interleaved case. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: 24-bit PCM is a perfectly legal and widely used depth that has no branch here, so it falls into the opaque waveformData array at line 81. RIFF WAVE requires this field to be a multiple of 8 for PCM.

FORMATCHUNK.wcbsize.description: Size in bytes of the format extension that follows; the template reads it only for DVI IMA ADPCM, where the extension is a single two-byte field.
FORMATCHUNK.wcbsize.algorithm: byte count of the format-specific extension bytes following this field
FORMATCHUNK.wcbsize.covers: the extension bytes after this field - for DVI IMA ADPCM just the two-byte wSamplesPerBlock; it excludes this field itself and the 16 bytes of common format fields before it

generation_range.rationale: For WAVE_FORMAT_DVI_ADPCM the extension is exactly the two-byte wSamplesPerBlock, so the only self-consistent value is 2. The template reads the two extension bytes unconditionally whatever this says, and dumps any remaining declared bytes into unknown[] at line 56, so a wrong value is invisible here and mis-sizes the chunk for a real decoder.

FORMATCHUNK.wcbsize.notes: Present only when wFormatTag is 17 (guard at line 45). This is the standard RIFF WAVE cbSize field, which every non-PCM format chunk carries; the template reads it only in the ADPCM branch, so for any other compressed tag the extension bytes land in unknown[] instead.

FORMATCHUNK.wSamplesPerBlock.description: Number of decoded sample frames each DVI IMA ADPCM block expands to; it is fixed by the block size and channel count rather than being free.
FORMATCHUNK.wSamplesPerBlock.algorithm: ((wBlockAlign - 4 * wChannels) * 8) / (wBitsPerSample * wChannels) + 1 - the ADPCM block carries a 4-byte per-channel preamble whose sample is counted, then packed nibbles
FORMATCHUNK.wSamplesPerBlock.covers: nothing itself; it describes how many sample frames one wBlockAlign-byte block of the data chunk decodes to

generation_range.rationale: Derived from the block alignment, so it is not free. IMA ADPCM blocks are conventionally 256, 512 or 1024 bytes, decoding to roughly twice that many mono samples. A value that disagrees with wBlockAlign makes every decoder produce the wrong number of samples.

FORMATCHUNK.wSamplesPerBlock.notes: Present only when wFormatTag is 17 (guard at line 45), which is the template's contribution: it establishes WHEN the field exists. The value formula itself is from the IMA/DVI ADPCM Recommended Practices - each block opens with a four-byte per-channel preamble whose sample is counted, then packed nibbles - and the template performs no check on it. The 1.2 history entry at line 12 records that this branch was added to 'correct parsing of DVI ADPCM'.

FORMATCHUNK.unknown.description: Any declared format-chunk bytes the template did not consume; its length is whatever the chunk size claims beyond what was actually read.
FORMATCHUNK.unknown.algorithm: byte count = FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize - (bytes consumed since the local pos captured at line 38, i.e. since just after the chunkSize field)
FORMATCHUNK.unknown.covers: the trailing format-chunk bytes after the fields the template understands, to the end of the chunk data

generation_range.rationale: For a plain PCM chunk this is 0; for WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE it is the 22 extension bytes the template never decodes - a two-byte cbSize, a two-byte valid-bits union, a four-byte channel mask and a sixteen-byte sub-format GUID. Emitted only when chunkSize exceeds what was read (guard at line 55), and the subtraction goes negative if chunkSize is smaller.

FORMATCHUNK.unknown.notes: This is where a WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE format chunk's entire extension ends up, including the sub-format GUID that names the real codec.

FORMATCHUNK.padding.description: Pad byte inserted after this chunk when its declared size is odd, so that the next chunk begins on an even boundary.
FORMATCHUNK.padding.notes: RIFF requires every chunk to occupy an even number of bytes, so a chunk whose declared size is odd is followed by a single pad byte that is NOT counted in chunkSize. The specification says the pad byte should be zero. Omitting it leaves every subsequent chunk misaligned by one byte, which is why the corruption risk is high even though the byte's value is ignored. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: this is the one padding branch in the file with no `FTell() < FileSize()` guard, so on a truncated file it reads past the end.

DATACHUNK.chunkID.description: The four-character chunk identifier that marks this as the wave data chunk; the top-level dispatch selects this struct only when the peeked tag equals it.

lookahead.note: The top-level chunk dispatch reads the four tag bytes by lookahead at line 535 and switches on them at line 538; the six recognised literals are at lines 540, 544, 548, 552, 556 and 560, and anything else falls to the default at line 564. Because the peek does not advance the file position, the same four bytes are then consumed as this struct's chunkID.

DATACHUNK.chunkID.notes: RIFF chunk identifiers are exactly four bytes of printable ASCII, space-padded when the name is shorter - which is why 'fmt ' and 'cue ' carry a trailing space that is part of the identifier and must be emitted. This chunk holds the actual audio samples and is mandatory in every WAVE file.

DATACHUNK.chunkSize.description: Byte count of this chunk's data, excluding the four identifier bytes and this size field itself and excluding any trailing pad byte.
DATACHUNK.chunkSize.algorithm: byte count of the sample data = number of sample frames * FORMATCHUNK.wBlockAlign; it must be an exact multiple of wBlockAlign
DATACHUNK.chunkSize.covers: the sample bytes following the size field, to the end of the chunk; it excludes the 'data' identifier, this size field and any pad byte

generation_range.rationale: This is the format's principal size lever: it is used directly as an array bound at lines 81 and 86 and as a divisor-numerator at lines 91, 96 and 108, with no upper check. A signed 32-bit value claims up to 2 GB of audio from four header bytes. 128 KB is roughly 1.5 seconds of 44.1 kHz stereo 16-bit audio and keeps generated files cheap while still producing a plausible sample stream.

DATACHUNK.chunkSize.notes: RIFF (Microsoft Multimedia Programming Interface and Data Specifications 1.0): every chunk is a four-character identifier, a 32-bit little-endian size, and that many data bytes, followed by a pad byte if the size is odd. The size counts neither the identifier nor itself nor the pad byte. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: declared as a SIGNED `long`, so a size above 2^31-1 reads negative and becomes a negative array bound. It must be an exact multiple of wBlockAlign; the guard at line 78 tests exactly that and falls back to an opaque byte array when it fails.

DATACHUNK.waveformData.description: The sample bytes read as an opaque array, used whenever the declared format is one the template cannot lay out as typed samples.
DATACHUNK.waveformData.covers: every byte of the data chunk payload

generation_range.rationale: Mirrors the chunkSize generation bound; this array is what a runaway size actually materialises as.

DATACHUNK.waveformData.notes: Reached by the guard at lines 77-78 whenever wBitsPerSample is not 8, 16 or 32, or wBlockAlign is 0, or chunkSize is not an exact multiple of wBlockAlign. For a compressed wFormatTag the bytes are a real codec stream - an IMA ADPCM block sequence, an MPEG elementary stream - and random bytes will not decode, though nothing rejects the file for it.

DATACHUNK.samples.description: The sample data laid out as typed samples; the element count and element type both follow from the format chunk, and the template has four different shapes for it.
DATACHUNK.samples.algorithm: element count = DATACHUNK.chunkSize for mono 8-bit, chunkSize/2 for mono 16-bit, chunkSize/4 for mono 32-bit, and chunkSize / FORMATCHUNK.wBlockAlign for every other channel count, where each element is one interleaved sample frame
DATACHUNK.samples.covers: every byte of the data chunk payload

generation_range.rationale: Element count. Bounded together with chunkSize: 64 K frames of 16-bit stereo is 256 KB. The count must never be chosen independently of chunkSize and wBlockAlign, because a real decoder recomputes it from those two fields.

DATACHUNK.samples.notes: Declared four times under the same name in mutually exclusive branches: lines 86, 91 and 96 are mono fast paths and line 108 is the general interleaved case. The individual sample VALUES are genuinely free audio data and deliberately have no constraints entries. Note the sign convention the specification imposes: 8-bit PCM samples are UNSIGNED with 128 as silence, while 16-bit and larger PCM samples are SIGNED two's complement with 0 as silence - and the template's `uchar` at line 86 and `short` at line 91 match that correctly.

DATACHUNK.padding.description: Pad byte inserted after this chunk when its declared size is odd, so that the next chunk begins on an even boundary.
DATACHUNK.padding.notes: RIFF requires every chunk to occupy an even number of bytes, so a chunk whose declared size is odd is followed by a single pad byte that is NOT counted in chunkSize. The specification says the pad byte should be zero. Omitting it leaves every subsequent chunk misaligned by one byte, which is why the corruption risk is high even though the byte's value is ignored. Guarded additionally by `FTell() < FileSize()` at line 112, so it is skipped at end of file.

SAMPLES.channels.description: One interleaved sample frame: exactly one sample per channel, laid out consecutively, with the element type following the bit depth.
SAMPLES.channels.algorithm: element count = FORMATCHUNK.wChannels; byte count = wChannels * wBitsPerSample / 8, which must equal FORMATCHUNK.wBlockAlign
SAMPLES.channels.covers: one sample frame of the data chunk payload

generation_range.rationale: Mirrors the wChannels generation bound; this array is emitted once per sample frame, so its size multiplies with the frame count.

SAMPLES.channels.notes: Declared three times under the same name at lines 103, 105 and 107 in mutually exclusive bit-depth branches. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: if wBitsPerSample is none of 8, 16 or 32 the struct emits NO field at all and every frame is zero bytes wide, which would spin the enclosing array - but the guard at line 77 makes that branch unreachable in practice. The byte size of this struct must equal wBlockAlign exactly, or the frame count computed at line 108 disagrees with the bytes present.

FACTCHUNK.chunkID.description: The four-character chunk identifier that marks this as the fact chunk; the top-level dispatch selects this struct only when the peeked tag equals it.

Because the peek does not advance the file position, the same four bytes are then consumed as this struct's chunkID.

FACTCHUNK.chunkID.notes: RIFF chunk identifiers are exactly four bytes of printable ASCII, space-padded when the name is shorter - which is why 'fmt ' and 'cue ' carry a trailing space that is part of the identifier and must be emitted. The fact chunk is required for every non-PCM format and states the decoded length, which a player cannot otherwise compute from a compressed data chunk.

FACTCHUNK.chunkSize.description: Byte count of this chunk's data, excluding the four identifier bytes and this size field itself and excluding any trailing pad byte.
FACTCHUNK.chunkSize.algorithm: byte count = 4 for the standard fact chunk, which carries only the uncompressed sample count
FACTCHUNK.chunkSize.covers: the uncompressedSize field that follows; it excludes the 'fact' identifier and this size field

generation_range.rationale: The specification defines the fact chunk as a single 32-bit value, so the only conforming size is 4. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: the template reads exactly one unsigned long whatever this field says and never skips to the declared end, so any other size desynchronises the chunk walk immediately - and unlike every other chunk here, FACTCHUNK has no padding branch at all, so an odd size leaves the parse permanently misaligned.

FACTCHUNK.chunkSize.notes: RIFF (Microsoft Multimedia Programming Interface and Data Specifications 1.0): every chunk is a four-character identifier, a 32-bit little-endian size, and that many data bytes, followed by a pad byte if the size is odd. The size counts neither the identifier nor itself nor the pad byte. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: declared as a SIGNED `long`, so a size above 2^31-1 reads negative and becomes a negative array bound.

FACTCHUNK.uncompressedSize.description: Number of sample frames the data chunk decodes to; for a compressed format this is the only way a player can know the true duration.
FACTCHUNK.uncompressedSize.algorithm: sample frame count = DATACHUNK.chunkSize / FORMATCHUNK.wBlockAlign for uncompressed PCM; for a compressed format it is the decoder's output frame count
FACTCHUNK.uncompressedSize.covers: nothing itself; it describes the decoded length of the data chunk payload

generation_range.rationale: Must agree with the data chunk's frame count; bounded together with DATACHUNK.chunkSize so the two stay consistent.

evidence.note: RIFF WAVE fact chunk: 'dwSampleLength - Number of samples (per channel).' The chunk is required for all compressed formats and for WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE, and its value must equal the number of sample frames the data chunk decodes to. The template reads a plain unsigned long and performs no check.

CUEPOINT.dwIdentifier.description: Unique identifier for this cue point; other chunks - notably smpl loops and adtl labels - refer back to it by this number.

generation_range.rationale: An identifier, not a magnitude. It must be unique among the cue points in the file and is the target of SMPLLOOPS.Cue_Point and of adtl labl/note/ltxt subchunks, so small sequential values are what real encoders write and what keeps the cross-references satisfiable.

evidence.note: RIFF WAVE cue chunk: 'dwIdentifier - Specifies the cue point name. Each <cue-point> record must have a unique dwIdentifier field.' The template reads a plain signed long and performs no check. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: declared `long`, which is signed, where the specification defines an unsigned 32-bit value.

CUEPOINT.dwPosition.description: Sample-frame offset of this cue point within the play order defined by the wavl playlist, or within the data chunk when there is no playlist.
CUEPOINT.dwPosition.algorithm: sample frame offset within the play order; when no playlist chunk is present it equals dwSampleOffset
CUEPOINT.dwPosition.covers: nothing itself; it locates a point in the decoded sample stream

generation_range.rationale: Must lie inside the sample stream, whose frame count is DATACHUNK.chunkSize divided by wBlockAlign; bounded together with the data chunk so cue points stay in range.

evidence.note: RIFF WAVE cue chunk: 'dwPosition - Specifies the sample position of the cue point ... the sample offset relative to the beginning of the play order as defined in the wavl chunk.' The template reads a plain signed long and performs no check.

CUEPOINT.fccChunk.description: Four-character identifier of the chunk this cue point refers into; only the two data-bearing chunk types can be named.
value_names: the data chunk holding the sample stream
a slnt silence chunk inside a wavl playlist

evidence.note: RIFF WAVE cue chunk: 'fccChunk - Specifies the four-character code that identifies the chunk containing the cue point ... This field is either data or slnt.' The template reads a plain char[4] and performs no check.

CUEPOINT.fccChunk.notes: Unlike a chunk identifier this field is a cross-reference, so its value must name a chunk that actually exists in the file.

CUEPOINT.dwChunkStart.description: Byte offset of the start of the chunk this cue point refers into, measured from the start of the wavl playlist; it is zero when there is no playlist.
CUEPOINT.dwChunkStart.algorithm: byte offset from the start of the wavl LIST chunk's data to the start of the referenced data or slnt chunk; 0 when the file has no wavl chunk
CUEPOINT.dwChunkStart.covers: nothing itself; it locates the chunk that contains the cue point

generation_range.rationale: The specification states this is zero when the file contains no wavl playlist chunk, which is the overwhelmingly common case and the only one this template can produce - it has no slnt or wavl handling at all. Any non-zero value would point into a structure that does not exist.

evidence.note: RIFF WAVE cue chunk: 'dwChunkStart - Specifies the byte offset of the start of the chunk containing the cue point ... This is a zero value if the file does not contain a wavl chunk.' The template reads a plain signed long and performs no check.

template_deviations.subject: every chunkSize declared as a signed long

template_deviations.subject: the top-level switch compares a char[4] against string literals
template_deviations.issue: `switch( tag )` at line 538 with `case "fmt ":` and the other five compares four raw bytes read by ReadBytes at line 535 against unterminated four-character literals.
template_deviations.impact: None for parsing, but it means the trailing space in 'fmt ' and 'cue ' is a significant byte, not padding: 'fmt' followed by a NUL would take the default branch and the file would then be rejected at line 70.
template_deviations.action: Emit the trailing space explicitly in both identifiers.

template_deviations.subject: SMPLLOOPS display functions mislabel their units
template_deviations.issue: WAV_SMPLLOOPS_Start at line 233 prints 'Loop Start at %u byte offset' and WAV_SMPLLOOPS_End at line 245 likewise, but the specification defines both fields in sample frames, not bytes.
template_deviations.impact: None for parsing - the fields are read correctly - but a generator following the display text would scale the values by the frame size and put every loop point in the wrong place.
template_deviations.action: Treat Start and End as sample frame indices.

template_deviations.subject: no validation beyond the RIFF/WAVE signature and the format-chunk presence check
template_deviations.issue: The guard at lines 523-527 and the one at lines 70-74 are the template's only two checks. wFormatTag, wChannels, dwSamplesPerSec, dwAvgBytesPerSec, wBitsPerSample, every chunk size, every cue and loop field and both reserved-by-convention values are read and accepted unexamined.
template_deviations.impact: The set of files this template accepts is very much larger than the set of valid WAVE files, so its behaviour is no guide to validity.
template_deviations.action: Take every 'spec'-sourced constraint in this file as binding despite the template's silence.
